## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

7	[Normal] 3. Alignment with NCAA guidance
8	[Normal] The NCAA Sports Science Institute has published guidance on the Responsible Use of Performance Technologies in College Athletics. That guidance is high-level by design, leaving each school to implement it according to its own needs and resources. This framework is Baylor Athletics' implementation.
9	[Normal] 4. Intended outcomes
10	[List Bullet] A consistent, shared understanding of the entire inventory of software and technology in use across the department.
11	[List Bullet] Improved utilization of what the department already owns.
12	[List Bullet] Coordinated renewal and term review, so the department stops discovering it is in the final year of an agreement with no time to act.

19	[Normal] 1.3  The request goes to the Business Office. The Business Office is the filter for all requests and is the first control point.
20	[Normal] 1.4 The forms are submitted to ITS for technical, security, and integration review. This is the second control point.
21	[Normal] 1.5 The request is evaluated against the Technology Evaluation Scorecard.
22	[Normal] 1.6  A request is disseminated for purchase only after clearing both control points. Declined requests are returned with documented reasons.
23	[Normal] 1.7  The Director of Applied holds a weekly standing meeting with the ITS representative to review the status of all open requests across all units.
24	[Normal] Phase 2 — Implementation and Product Use
25	[Normal] 2.1  A project manager is assigned. This may be administrative staff other than the Dir App, depending on the unit and the system.
26	[Normal] 2.2 Status flows from the weekly ITS standing meeting through the Dir App to the assigned project manager and stakeholders, so that every open request has a known owner.
27	[Normal] 2.3  Open requests are tracked as follows: project, item, requester, project manager, date submitted, desired implementation date, current status, and what is holding it up.

32	[Normal] 3.4  The outcome is renew, modify or renegotiate, or discontinue.
33	[Normal] 7. Review depth scales to risk
34	[Normal] Not every request warrants the same scrutiny. Three tiers:
35	[Normal] 8. Exceptions
36	[Normal] 8.1  Urgent and “emergency” requests
37	[Normal] An expedited lane, not a bypass. Urgent requests clear the same control points on a compressed clock, with a short risk checklist completed at intake to surface issues that would otherwise delay the request: data category, contract term, integration dependency, and whether athlete data leaves Baylor.
38	[Normal] 8.2  Product trials and pilots
39	[Normal] Trials run under provisional approval in a contained environment:
40	[List Bullet] A defined start and hard end date, agreed at approval.
41	[List Bullet] No physiologic data and no identifiable athlete data until full approval.
42	[List Bullet] A named owner and a stated question the trial is meant to answer.

  | ITS | Second control point. Technical, security, and integration review; confirms the system can be supported.
  | Director of Applied Performance | Single point of contact and facilitator. Holds the weekly standing meeting with ITS and relays status to project managers and stakeholders.
  | Assigned Project Manager | Owns delivery of the individual project. May be administrative staff other than Dir of Applied.
  | Sport Administrator | Signs off on renewal decisions at Phase 3, informed by the usage review.
  | Health & Wellness / Medical | Reviews requests involving physiologic or health data.
  --- END TABLE ---
[Normal] 6. The three phases
[Normal] Phase 1 — Proposal, Approval, Purchase
[Normal] 1.1  A request is initiated by the Director of Applied Performance, a Head Coach, or any Admin Unit Director.
[Normal] 1.2  The requester completes the Technology Idea Form and the internal ATH Form. The request must declare its data category and proposed review tier.
[Normal] 1.3  The request goes to the Business Office. The Business Office is the filter for all requests and is the first control point.
[Normal] 1.4 The forms are submitted to ITS for technical, security, and integration review. This is the second control point.
[Normal] 1.5 The request is evaluated against the Technology Evaluation Scorecard.
[Normal] 1.6  A request is disseminated for purchase only after clearing both control points. Declined requests are returned with documented reasons.
[Normal] 1.7  The Director of Applied holds a weekly standing meeting with the ITS representative to review the status of all open requests across all units.
[Normal] Phase 2 — Implementation and Product Use
[Normal] 2.1  A project manager is assigned. This may be administrative staff other than the Dir App, depending on the unit and the system.
[Normal] 2.2 Status flows from the weekly ITS standing meeting through the Dir App to the assigned project manager and stakeholders, so that every open request has a known owner.
[Normal] 2.3  Open requests are tracked as follows: project, item, requester, project manager, date submitted, desired implementation date, current status, and what is holding it up.
[Normal] Phase 3 — Product Review and Renewal Decision
[Normal] 3.1 Review is triggered at six months, or at the end of the competitive season, whichever is longer. Tools used primarily in season are therefore judged on in-season usage.
[Normal] 3.2  The review compares actual utilization against the intent stated on the original request.
[Normal] 3.3  Low utilization opens a diagnostic conversation before a renewal conclusion.
[Normal] 3.4  The outcome is renew, modify or renegotiate, or discontinue.
[Normal] 7. Review depth scales to risk
[Normal] Not every request warrants the same scrutiny. Three tiers:
  --- TABLE ---
  | Tier | Trigger | Review depth
  | Light | No athlete data; single unit; low or one-time cost | Compliance, Privacy, Ownership, Transparency, Interoperability
  | Standard | Performance data, multi-team use, or recurring cost | Full review
  | Elevated | Physiologic or health data; external data sharing; third-party processing of athlete data | Full review, plus data protection review and Health & Wellness / medical sign-off
  --- END TABLE ---
[Normal] 8. Exceptions
[Normal] 8.1  Urgent and “emergency” requests
[Normal] An expedited lane, not a bypass. Urgent requests clear the same control points on a compressed clock, with a short risk checklist completed at intake to surface issues that would otherwise delay the request: data category, contract term, integration dependency, and whether athlete data leaves Baylor.
[Normal] 8.2  Product trials and pilots
[Normal] Trials run under provisional approval in a contained environment:
[List Bullet] A defined start and hard end date, agreed at approval.
[List Bullet] No physiologic data and no identifiable athlete data until full approval.
[List Bullet] A named owner and a stated question the trial is meant to answer.
[List Bullet] A mandatory review at the end of the trial that converts to full approval or terminates. A trial that continues has become a purchase without a decision.

# /// script
# dependencies = ["python-docx"]
# ///
"""
Build the merged Software and Technology Management Framework.

Base skeleton : deliverables/Software_and_Tech_Management_DRAFT_ER_.docx  (Aug 11)
Merged in     : JA_TechPolicy.pdf sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8
Excluded      : JA sections 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 and Appendices A-D
Scope         : department-wide (all Athletics technology), athlete performance
                technology as originating context and highest-risk tier
"""
import copy
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor, Emu
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

SRC = "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/Software_and_Tech_Management_DRAFT_ER_.docx"
DIAGRAM = "/Users/kristinarash/.claude/jobs/126c5de4/tmp/dia/diagram_aug11.png"
OUT = "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/Software_and_Tech_Management_MERGED_ER_2026-08-11.docx"

FONT = "Aptos"
BAYLOR_GREEN = "154734"
GOLD = "FFB81C"

doc = Document()

# ---- page setup: match source (8.5x11, 0.5in margins) ----
s = doc.sections[0]
s.page_width, s.page_height = Emu(7772400), Emu(10058400)
s.left_margin = s.right_margin = s.top_margin = s.bottom_margin = Emu(457200)

normal = doc.styles["Normal"]
normal.font.name = FONT
normal.font.size = Pt(10.5)
normal.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), FONT)
normal.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
normal.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)


def _shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def para(text="", size=10.5, bold=False, italic=False, color=None,
         space_before=0, space_after=6, style=None, align=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    if text:
        r = p.add_run(text)
        r.font.name = FONT
        r.font.size = Pt(size)
        r.font.bold = bold
        r.font.italic = italic
        if color:
            r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
    return p


def h1(text):
    return para(text, size=13, bold=True, color=BAYLOR_GREEN,
                space_before=14, space_after=6)


def h2(text):
    return para(text, size=11.5, bold=True, color=BAYLOR_GREEN,
                space_before=10, space_after=4)


def bullet(text, size=10.5):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.font.name = FONT
    r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p


def table(headers, rows, widths=None):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    hdr = t.rows[0]
    for i, htext in enumerate(headers):
        cell = hdr.cells[i]
        cell.text = ""
        p = cell.paragraphs[0]
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
        r = p.add_run(htext)
        r.font.name = FONT
        r.font.size = Pt(9.5)
        r.font.bold = True
        r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("FFFFFF")
        _shade(cell, BAYLOR_GREEN)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, val in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            r = p.add_run(val)
            r.font.name = FONT
            r.font.size = Pt(9.5)
            if i == 0 and len(headers) > 1:
                r.font.bold = True
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    # spacing after table
    para("", space_after=2)
    return t


# =====================================================================
# TITLE
# =====================================================================
para("Software and Technology Management Framework", size=19, bold=True,
     color=BAYLOR_GREEN, space_after=2)
para("Baylor Athletics  |  Draft for discussion", size=10.5, italic=True,
     color="595959", space_after=12)

# =====================================================================
# 1. PURPOSE   (ours + JA 1 Policy Statement + JA 2 Reason for the Policy)
# =====================================================================
h1("1. Purpose")

para("To increase the efficiency and timeliness of requests for software and technology "
     "purchase and implementation, and to establish a consistent, transparent process for "
     "how those decisions are made, reviewed, and renewed.")

h2("1.1  Policy statement")
para("Baylor Athletics shall select, acquire, implement, use, access, disclose, retain, and "
     "dispose of software, technology, and the data they generate only for authorized "
     "athletics, sports medicine, health, safety, performance, compliance, and operational "
     "purposes, and only in accordance with Baylor University policies, applicable law, NCAA "
     "guidance, contractual obligations, and approved data-governance practices.")
para("Software and technology must be governed through a written plan, routine education, "
     "defined data rights, structured technology review, and continuous improvement.")

h2("1.2  Reason for the framework")
para("Technology used in athletics may collect biometric, health-related, performance, "
     "workload, recovery, video, sensor, survey, software, mobile-application, and other "
     "individual-level data. Responsible use of these technologies requires coordination "
     "across Athletics, Sports Medicine, Information Technology Services, Privacy, Legal, "
     "Compliance, Procurement, and Records Management. No single unit can carry the decision "
     "alone, and no request should reach a signature without those perspectives having been "
     "applied in a known order.")
para("This framework is intended to help Baylor Athletics support student-athlete health, "
     "safety, privacy, autonomy, data security, and performance while reducing legal, "
     "regulatory, contractual, operational, and reputational risk.")
para("The framework originates in the context of athlete performance technology, where the "
     "stakes attached to the data are highest and where NCAA guidance is most explicit. It is "
     "written, however, as the department's general approach to how all technology is "
     "assessed. The process below applies to every technology request in the department; the "
     "depth of review scales to the risk the request actually carries, as set out in Section 6.")

# =====================================================================
# 2. SCOPE AND TERMINOLOGY  (ours + JA 3 Affected + JA 4 Exclusions + JA 6 Definitions)
# =====================================================================
h1("2. Scope and terminology")

h2("2.1  Scope")
para("Technology refers to tangible items like devices, wearables, equipment, and "
     "applications. Software refers to the platforms and systems those items connect to. The "
     "two are rarely purchased independently, and this framework covers both.")
para("The framework is department-wide. It is not limited to performance, health and "
     "wellness, or any single unit. Athlete performance technology is a subset within that "
     "scope, and it is the subset that triggers the deepest review, but a request carrying no "
     "athlete data is still a request and still moves through the same two control points.")

h2("2.2  Individuals and entities affected")
bullet("Baylor Athletics staff, coaches, sports medicine personnel, strength and conditioning "
       "staff, analysts, administrators, student support staff, and other Baylor personnel who "
       "select, use, access, interpret, or disclose technology and the data it generates.")
bullet("Student-athletes whose data is collected, used, analyzed, inferred, stored, or "
       "disclosed through these technologies.")
bullet("Vendors, contractors, consultants, and other third parties that collect, store, "
       "process, analyze, host, transmit, or receive Baylor Athletics data on Baylor's behalf.")
bullet("Baylor units supporting Athletics, including ITS, Information Security, Office of "
       "General Counsel, University Compliance and Risk Services, Privacy, Internal Audit, "
       "Procurement, and records-management functions.")

h2("2.3  Exclusions")
para("This framework does not replace or supersede Baylor policies that already govern "
     "specific categories of data, systems, conduct, records, or legal obligations. Where a "
     "more specific Baylor policy applies, that policy continues to govern. This document "
     "should be read as an Athletics-specific overlay that routes technology decisions into "
     "existing Baylor governance channels rather than around them.")

h2("2.4  Definitions")
table(
    ["Term", "Definition for this framework"],
    [
        ("Technology",
         "Tangible items such as devices, wearables, sensors, cameras, and equipment, together "
         "with the applications that operate them."),
        ("Software",
         "The platforms and systems that technology connects to, including hosted, cloud, and "
         "on-premises applications."),
        ("Athlete Performance Technology",
         "Any device, sensor, wearable, software, mobile application, camera, survey, analytics "
         "platform, AI-enabled system, or other technology used to collect, infer, monitor, "
         "analyze, store, or communicate biometric, performance, workload, recovery, wellness, "
         "health, safety, training, competition, or related data about student-athletes."),
        ("Athlete Performance Technology Data",
         "Data collected, generated, inferred, stored, analyzed, or disclosed through athlete "
         "performance technologies, including performance metrics, physiological metrics, sleep, "
         "hydration, nutrition, stress indicators, recovery, training load, practice or game "
         "analytics, and related data."),
        ("Restricted / Protected Data",
         "Data subject to Baylor data-classification requirements and heightened safeguards, "
         "including where applicable PHI, FERPA records, biometric identifiers, credentials, "
         "SSNs, financial information, IRB-related research data, and other regulated or "
         "sensitive data."),
        ("Medical Decision-Making Data",
         "Data used, intended to be used, or reasonably likely to be used to inform medical "
         "management, injury evaluation, treatment, rehabilitation, or return-to-play decisions."),
        ("Approved Use Case",
         "A documented and approved purpose, user population, data category, vendor or system, "
         "and data lifecycle for a technology."),
        ("Student-Athlete Notice",
         "A plain-language explanation to student-athletes of what data is collected, why, who "
         "may access it, permissible uses, retention, rights, questions, and concerns."),
    ],
    widths=[1.9, 5.6],
)

# =====================================================================
# 3. ALIGNMENT WITH NCAA GUIDANCE   (ours, unchanged)
# =====================================================================
h1("3. Alignment with NCAA guidance")
para("The NCAA Sports Science Institute has published guidance on the Responsible Use of "
     "Performance Technologies in College Athletics. That guidance is high-level by design, "
     "leaving each school to implement it according to its own needs and resources. This "
     "framework is Baylor Athletics' implementation.")

# =====================================================================
# 4. INTENDED OUTCOMES   (ours, unchanged)
# =====================================================================
h1("4. Intended outcomes")
bullet("A consistent, shared understanding of the entire inventory of software and technology "
       "in use across the department.")
bullet("Improved utilization of what the department already owns.")
bullet("Coordinated renewal and term review, so the department stops discovering it is in the "
       "final year of an agreement with no time to act.")
bullet("Increased staff fluency so sport administrators and unit staff can speak to technology "
       "questions rather than defaulting on whatever is asked for in the moment.")

# =====================================================================
# 5. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES   (our Roles table + JA 8 Responsibilities)
# =====================================================================
h1("5. Roles and responsibilities")
para("The roles below combine the operating roles that move a request through the process with "
     "the review functions that must be applied before a request can clear.")
table(
    ["Role", "Responsibility in this framework"],
    [
        ("Head Coach, Admin, and/or Unit Director",
         "Initiates the request. Completes the Idea Form and internal ATH Form, including the "
         "declared data category and proposed review tier."),
        ("Athletics Executive Sponsor",
         "Owns Athletics operational compliance with this framework and ensures teams, coaches, "
         "and staff use approved technologies and approved use cases."),
        ("Business Office",
         "First control point. Filters all requests before they proceed. Budget, contract, and "
         "duplication check process through the Business Office."),
        ("ITS / Information Security",
         "Second control point. Technical, security, and integration review; confirms the system "
         "can be supported. Reviews access, authentication, storage, transmission, monitoring, "
         "incident response, and security controls."),
        ("Director of Applied Performance",
         "Single point of contact and facilitator. Holds the weekly standing meeting with ITS "
         "and relays status to project managers and stakeholders. Facilitator, not owner; not "
         "the subject-matter expert and not the project manager."),
        ("Assigned Project Manager",
         "Owns delivery of the individual project. May be administrative staff other than the "
         "Director of Applied Performance."),
        ("Sport Administrator",
         "Signs off on renewal decisions at Phase 3, informed by the usage review."),
        ("Health & Wellness / Sports Medicine",
         "Reviews requests involving physiologic or health data. Must be involved where data may "
         "inform medical decision-making, injury evaluation, rehabilitation, or return-to-play "
         "decisions."),
        ("Athletics Compliance",
         "Coordinates NCAA, conference, student-athlete, and departmental compliance "
         "implications."),
        ("Office of General Counsel / Privacy",
         "Reviews FERPA, HIPAA, Texas privacy, consent, data rights, disclosure, vendor terms, "
         "and legal holds."),
        ("Procurement / Contracting",
         "Ensures vendor contracts address ownership, permitted use, storage, access, data "
         "sharing, AI training, automated decision-making, downstream sharing, retention, "
         "deletion, portability, and breach notification."),
        ("Coaches, Staff, and Users",
         "Use technology only for approved purposes, complete required training, avoid "
         "unauthorized disclosure, and report suspected misuse or incidents."),
        ("Student-Athlete Representatives",
         "Provide feedback on transparency, education, perceived benefits, and potential "
         "unintended impacts of technology use."),
    ],
    widths=[2.1, 5.4],
)

# =====================================================================
# 6. REVIEW DEPTH SCALES TO RISK   (ours, was section 7)
# =====================================================================
h1("6. Review depth scales to risk")
para("Not every request warrants the same scrutiny. Three tiers:")
table(
    ["Tier", "Trigger", "Review depth"],
    [
        ("Light", "No athlete data; single unit; low or one-time cost",
         "Compliance, Privacy, Ownership, Transparency, Interoperability"),
        ("Standard", "Performance data, multi-team use, or recurring cost", "Full review"),
        ("Elevated",
         "Physiologic or health data; external data sharing; third-party processing of athlete "
         "data",
         "Full review, plus data protection review and Health & Wellness / medical sign-off"),
    ],
    widths=[0.9, 3.0, 3.6],
)
para("The tier is proposed by the requester at intake and confirmed at the control points. A "
     "request that changes character during review — a tool that turns out to touch physiologic "
     "data, or a single-team pilot that becomes a department purchase — is re-tiered rather "
     "than carried forward at its original depth.")

# =====================================================================
# 7. EXCEPTIONS   (ours, was section 8; 8.2 remains deleted per Aug 11 draft)
# =====================================================================
h1("7. Exceptions")
h2("7.1  Urgent and “emergency” requests")
para("An expedited lane, not a bypass. Urgent requests clear the same control points on a "
     "compressed clock, with a short risk checklist completed at intake to surface issues that "
     "would otherwise delay the request: data category, contract term, integration dependency, "
     "and whether athlete data leaves Baylor.")

# =====================================================================
# 8. THE THREE PHASES   (ours, was section 6; moved last as directed)
# =====================================================================
h1("8. The three phases")

h2("Phase 1 — Proposal, Approval, Purchase")
for t in [
    "1.1  A request is initiated by the Director of Applied Performance, a Head Coach, or any Admin Unit Director.",
    "1.2  The requester completes the Technology Idea Form and the internal ATH Form. The request must declare its data category and proposed review tier.",
    "1.3  The request goes to the Business Office. The Business Office serves as the filter for all requests and the first control point.",
    "1.4  The forms are submitted to ITS for technical, security, and integration review. This is the second control point.",
    "1.5  The request is evaluated against the Technology Evaluation Scorecard.",
    "1.6  A request is disseminated for purchase only after clearing both control points. Declined requests are returned with documented reasons.",
    "1.7  The Director of Applied holds a weekly standing meeting with the ITS representative to review the status of all open requests across all units.",
]:
    para(t, space_after=4)

h2("Phase 2 — Implementation and Product Use")
for t in [
    "2.1  A project manager is assigned. This may be administrative staff other than the Dir App, depending on the unit and the system.",
    "2.2  Status flows from the weekly ITS standing meeting through the Dir App to the assigned project manager and stakeholders, so that every open request has a known owner.",
    "2.3  Open requests are tracked as follows: project, item, requester, project manager, date submitted, desired implementation date, current status, and what is holding it up.",
]:
    para(t, space_after=4)

h2("Phase 3 — Product Review and Renewal Decision")
for t in [
    "3.1  Review is triggered at six months, or at the end of the competitive season, whichever is longer. Tools used primarily in season are therefore judged on in-season usage.",
    "3.2  The review compares actual utilization against the intent stated on the original request.",
    "3.3  Low utilization opens a diagnostic conversation before a renewal conclusion.",
    "3.4  The outcome is renew, modify or renegotiate, or discontinue.",
]:
    para(t, space_after=4)

# =====================================================================
# 9. WORKFLOW   (diagram)
# =====================================================================
doc.add_page_break()
h1("9. Workflow")
pic_p = doc.add_paragraph()
pic_p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
pic_p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
pic_p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
pic_p.add_run().add_picture(DIAGRAM, height=Inches(9.0))

doc.save(OUT)
print("WROTE:", OUT)

def _shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def para(text="", size=10.5, bold=False, italic=False, color=None,
         space_before=0, space_after=6, style=None, align=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    if text:
        r = p.add_run(text)
        r.font.name = FONT
        r.font.size = Pt(size)
        r.font.bold = bold
        r.font.italic = italic
        if color:
            r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
    return p


def h1(text):
    return para(text, size=13, bold=True, color=BAYLOR_GREEN,
                space_before=14, space_after=6)


def h2(text):
    return para(text, size=11.5, bold=True, color=BAYLOR_GREEN,
                space_before=10, space_after=4)


def bullet(text, size=10.5):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.font.name = FONT
    r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p


def table(headers, rows, widths=None):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    hdr = t.rows[0]
    for i, htext in enumerate(headers):
        cell = hdr.cells[i]
        cell.text = ""
        p = cell.paragraphs[0]
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
        r = p.add_run(htext)
        r.font.name = FONT
        r.font.size = Pt(9.5)
        r.font.bold = True
        r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("FFFFFF")
        _shade(cell, BAYLOR_GREEN)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, val in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            r = p.add_run(val)
            r.font.name = FONT
            r.font.size = Pt(9.5)
            if i == 0 and len(headers) > 1:
                r.font.bold = True
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    # spacing after table
    para("", space_after=2)
    return t


# =====================================================================
# TITLE
# =====================================================================
para("Software and Technology Management Framework", size=19, bold=True,
     color=BAYLOR_GREEN, space_after=2)
para("Baylor Athletics  |  Draft for discussion", size=10.5, italic=True,
     color="595959", space_after=12)

# =====================================================================
# 1. PURPOSE   (ours + JA 1 Policy Statement + JA 2 Reason for the Policy)
# =====================================================================
h1("1. Purpose")

para("To increase the efficiency and timeliness of requests for software and technology "
     "purchase and implementation, and to establish a consistent, transparent process for "
     "how those decisions are made, reviewed, and renewed.")

h2("1.1  Policy statement")
para("Baylor Athletics shall select, acquire, implement, use, access, disclose, retain, and "
     "dispose of software, technology, and the data they generate only for authorized "
     "athletics, sports medicine, health, safety, performance, compliance, and operational "
     "purposes, and only in accordance with Baylor University policies, applicable law, NCAA "
     "guidance, contractual obligations, and approved data-governance practices.")
para("Software and technology must be governed through a written plan, routine education, "
     "defined data rights, structured technology review, and continuous improvement.")

h2("1.2  Reason for the framework")
para("Technology used in athletics may collect biometric, health-related, performance, "
     "workload, recovery, video, sensor, survey, software, mobile-application, and other "
     "individual-level data. Responsible use of these technologies requires coordination "
     "across Athletics, Sports Medicine, Information Technology Services, Privacy, Legal, "
     "Compliance, Procurement, and Records Management. No single unit can carry the decision "
     "alone, and no request should reach a signature without those perspectives having been "
     "applied in a known order.")
para("This framework is intended to help Baylor Athletics support student-athlete health, "
     "safety, privacy, autonomy, data security, and performance while reducing legal, "
     "regulatory, contractual, operational, and reputational risk.")
para("The framework originates in the context of athlete performance technology, where the "
     "stakes attached to the data are highest and where NCAA guidance is most explicit. It is "
     "written, however, as the department's general approach to how all technology is "
     "assessed. The process below applies to every technology request in the department; the "
     "depth of review scales to the risk the request actually carries, as set out in Section 6.")

# =====================================================================
# 2. SCOPE AND TERMINOLOGY  (ours + JA 3 Affected + JA 4 Exclusions + JA 6 Definitions)
# =====================================================================
h1("2. Scope and terminology")

h2("2.1  Scope")
para("Technology refers to tangible items like devices, wearables, equipment, and "
     "applications. Software refers to the platforms and systems those items connect to. The "
     "two are rarely purchased independently, and this framework covers both.")
para("The framework is department-wide. It is not limited to performance, health and "
     "wellness, or any single unit. Athlete performance technology is a subset within that "
     "scope, and it is the subset that triggers the deepest review, but a request carrying no "
     "athlete data is still a request and still moves through the same two control points.")

h2("2.2  Individuals and entities affected")
bullet("Baylor Athletics staff, coaches, sports medicine personnel, strength and conditioning "
       "staff, analysts, administrators, student support staff, and other Baylor personnel who "
       "select, use, access, interpret, or disclose technology and the data it generates.")
bullet("Student-athletes whose data is collected, used, analyzed, inferred, stored, or "
       "disclosed through these technologies.")
bullet("Vendors, contractors, consultants, and other third parties that collect, store, "
       "process, analyze, host, transmit, or receive Baylor Athletics data on Baylor's behalf.")
bullet("Baylor units supporting Athletics, including ITS, Information Security, Office of "
       "General Counsel, University Compliance and Risk Services, Privacy, Internal Audit, "
       "Procurement, and records-management functions.")

h2("2.3  Exclusions")
para("This framework does not replace or supersede Baylor policies that already govern "
     "specific categories of data, systems, conduct, records, or legal obligations. Where a "
     "more specific Baylor policy applies, that policy continues to govern. This document "
     "should be read as an Athletics-specific overlay that routes technology decisions into "
     "existing Baylor governance channels rather than around them.")

h2("2.4  Definitions")
table(
    ["Term", "Definition for this framework"],
    [
        ("Technology",
         "Tangible items such as devices, wearables, sensors, cameras, and equipment, together "
         "with the applications that operate them."),
        ("Software",
         "The platforms and systems that technology connects to, including hosted, cloud, and "
         "on-premises applications."),
        ("Athlete Performance Technology",
         "Any device, sensor, wearable, software, mobile application, camera, survey, analytics "
         "platform, AI-enabled system, or other technology used to collect, infer, monitor, "
         "analyze, store, or communicate biometric, performance, workload, recovery, wellness, "
         "health, safety, training, competition, or related data about student-athletes."),
        ("Athlete Performance Technology Data",
         "Data collected, generated, inferred, stored, analyzed, or disclosed through athlete "
         "performance technologies, including performance metrics, physiological metrics, sleep, "
         "hydration, nutrition, stress indicators, recovery, training load, practice or game "
         "analytics, and related data."),
        ("Restricted / Protected Data",
         "Data subject to Baylor data-classification requirements and heightened safeguards, "
         "including where applicable PHI, FERPA records, biometric identifiers, credentials, "
         "SSNs, financial information, IRB-related research data, and other regulated or "
         "sensitive data."),
        ("Medical Decision-Making Data",
         "Data used, intended to be used, or reasonably likely to be used to inform medical "
         "management, injury evaluation, treatment, rehabilitation, or return-to-play decisions."),
        ("Approved Use Case",
         "A documented and approved purpose, user population, data category, vendor or system, "
         "and data lifecycle for a technology."),
        ("Student-Athlete Notice",
         "A plain-language explanation to student-athletes of what data is collected, why, who "
         "may access it, permissible uses, retention, rights, questions, and concerns."),
    ],
    widths=[1.9, 5.6],
)

# =====================================================================
# 3. ALIGNMENT WITH NCAA GUIDANCE   (ours, unchanged)
# =====================================================================
h1("3. Alignment with NCAA guidance")
para("The NCAA Sports Science Institute has published guidance on the Responsible Use of "
     "Performance Technologies in College Athletics. That guidance is high-level by design, "
     "leaving each school to implement it according to its own needs and resources. This "
     "framework is Baylor Athletics' implementation.")

# =====================================================================
# 4. INTENDED OUTCOMES   (ours, unchanged)
# =====================================================================
h1("4. Intended outcomes")
bullet("A consistent, shared understanding of the entire inventory of software and technology "
       "in use across the department.")
bullet("Improved utilization of what the department already owns.")
bullet("Coordinated renewal and term review, so the department stops discovering it is in the "
       "final year of an agreement with no time to act.")
bullet("Increased staff fluency so sport administrators and unit staff can speak to technology "
       "questions rather than defaulting on whatever is asked for in the moment.")

# =====================================================================
# 5. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES   (our Roles table + JA 8 Responsibilities)
# =====================================================================
h1("5. Roles and responsibilities")
para("The roles below combine the operating roles that move a request through the process with "
     "the review functions that must be applied before a request can clear.")
table(
    ["Role", "Responsibility in this framework"],
    [
        ("Head Coach, Admin, and/or Unit Director",
         "Initiates the request. Completes the Idea Form and internal ATH Form, including the "
         "declared data category and proposed review tier."),
        ("Athletics Executive Sponsor",
         "Owns Athletics operational compliance with this framework and ensures teams, coaches, "
         "and staff use approved technologies and approved use cases."),
        ("Business Office",
         "First control point. Filters all requests before they proceed. Budget, contract, and "
         "duplication check process through the Business Office."),
        ("ITS / Information Security",
         "Second control point. Technical, security, and integration review; confirms the system "
         "can be supported. Reviews access, authentication, storage, transmission, monitoring, "
         "incident response, and security controls."),
        ("Director of Applied Performance",
         "Single point of contact and facilitator. Holds the weekly standing meeting with ITS "
         "and relays status to project managers and stakeholders. Facilitator, not owner; not "
         "the subject-matter expert and not the project manager."),
        ("Assigned Project Manager",
         "Owns delivery of the individual project. May be administrative staff other than the "
         "Director of Applied Performance."),
        ("Sport Administrator",
         "Signs off on renewal decisions at Phase 3, informed by the usage review."),
        ("Health & Wellness / Sports Medicine",
         "Reviews requests involving physiologic or health data. Must be involved where data may "
         "inform medical decision-making, injury evaluation, rehabilitation, or return-to-play "
         "decisions."),
        ("Athletics Compliance",
         "Coordinates NCAA, conference, student-athlete, and departmental compliance "
         "implications."),
        ("Office of General Counsel / Privacy",
         "Reviews FERPA, HIPAA, Texas privacy, consent, data rights, disclosure, vendor terms, "
         "and legal holds."),
        ("Procurement / Contracting",
         "Ensures vendor contracts address ownership, permitted use, storage, access, data "
         "sharing, AI training, automated decision-making, downstream sharing, retention, "
         "deletion, portability, and breach notification."),
        ("Coaches, Staff, and Users",
         "Use technology only for approved purposes, complete required training, avoid "
         "unauthorized disclosure, and report suspected misuse or incidents."),
        ("Student-Athlete Representatives",
         "Provide feedback on transparency, education, perceived benefits, and potential "
         "unintended impacts of technology use."),
    ],
    widths=[2.1, 5.4],
)

# =====================================================================
# 6. REVIEW DEPTH SCALES TO RISK   (ours, was section 7)
# =====================================================================
h1("6. Review depth scales to risk")
para("Not every request warrants the same scrutiny. Three tiers:")
table(
    ["Tier", "Trigger", "Review depth"],
    [
        ("Light", "No athlete data; single unit; low or one-time cost",
         "Compliance, Privacy, Ownership, Transparency, Interoperability"),
        ("Standard", "Performance data, multi-team use, or recurring cost", "Full review"),
        ("Elevated",
         "Physiologic or health data; external data sharing; third-party processing of athlete "
         "data",
         "Full review, plus data protection review and Health & Wellness / medical sign-off"),
    ],
    widths=[0.9, 3.0, 3.6],
)
para("The tier is proposed by the requester at intake and confirmed at the control points. A "
     "request that changes character during review — a tool that turns out to touch physiologic "
     "data, or a single-team pilot that becomes a department purchase — is re-tiered rather "
     "than carried forward at its original depth.")

# =====================================================================
# 7. EXCEPTIONS   (ours, was section 8; 8.2 remains deleted per Aug 11 draft)
# =====================================================================
h1("7. Exceptions")
h2("7.1  Urgent and “emergency” requests")
para("An expedited lane, not a bypass. Urgent requests clear the same control points on a "
     "compressed clock, with a short risk checklist completed at intake to surface issues that "
     "would otherwise delay the request: data category, contract term, integration dependency, "
     "and whether athlete data leaves Baylor.")

# =====================================================================
# 8. THE THREE PHASES   (ours, was section 6; moved last as directed)
# =====================================================================
h1("8. The three phases")

h2("Phase 1 — Proposal, Approval, Purchase")
for t in [
    "1.1  A request is initiated by the Director of Applied Performance, a Head Coach, or any Admin Unit Director.",
    "1.2  The requester completes the Technology Idea Form and the internal ATH Form. The request must declare its data category and proposed review tier.",
    "1.3  The request goes to the Business Office. The Business Office serves as the filter for all requests and the first control point.",
    "1.4  The forms are submitted to ITS for technical, security, and integration review. This is the second control point.",
    "1.5  The request is evaluated against the Technology Evaluation Scorecard.",
    "1.6  A request is disseminated for purchase only after clearing both control points. Declined requests are returned with documented reasons.",
    "1.7  The Director of Applied holds a weekly standing meeting with the ITS representative to review the status of all open requests across all units.",
]:
    para(t, space_after=4)

h2("Phase 2 — Implementation and Product Use")
for t in [
    "2.1  A project manager is assigned. This may be administrative staff other than the Dir App, depending on the unit and the system.",
    "2.2  Status flows from the weekly ITS standing meeting through the Dir App to the assigned project manager and stakeholders, so that every open request has a known owner.",
    "2.3  Open requests are tracked as follows: project, item, requester, project manager, date submitted, desired implementation date, current status, and what is holding it up.",
]:
    para(t, space_after=4)

h2("Phase 3 — Product Review and Renewal Decision")
for t in [
    "3.1  Review is triggered at six months, or at the end of the competitive season, whichever is longer. Tools used primarily in season are therefore judged on in-season usage.",
    "3.2  The review compares actual utilization against the intent stated on the original request.",
    "3.3  Low utilization opens a diagnostic conversation before a renewal conclusion.",
    "3.4  The outcome is renew, modify or renegotiate, or discontinue.",
]:
    para(t, space_after=4)

# =====================================================================
# 9. WORKFLOW   (diagram)
# =====================================================================
doc.add_page_break()
h1("9. Workflow")
pic_p = doc.add_paragraph()
pic_p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
pic_p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
pic_p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
pic_p.add_run().add_picture(DIAGRAM, height=Inches(9.0))

doc.save(OUT)
print("WROTE:", OUT)

# /// script
# dependencies = ["pillow"]
# ///
"""
Replace 'tier' with 'level' in the two workflow-diagram labels, so the diagram
matches Section 6 ('Levels of review') and Phase 1.2 ('proposed review level').

The word 'level' is neutral to whatever tier naming is finally chosen, so this
change survives the naming discussion.

Method: the PNG is an exact 3x export of the .excalidraw with 10px padding, so
JSON coords map to pixels as px = (x-30)*3, py = (y-10)*3. Each label is
re-rendered in the original font (Cascadia Code) and re-centred on the same
centre line, calibrated against the existing ink so size/baseline match.
"""
import json
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

SRC_PNG = "dia/diagram_aug11.png"
OUT_PNG = "dia/diagram_level.png"
EXCAL = "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/Framework.excalidraw"
FONT = "cascadia_font/ttf/static/CascadiaCode-Regular.ttf"

SCALE = 3
PAD = 10
MINX, MINY = 40, 20


def to_px(x, y):
    return (x - MINX + PAD) * SCALE, (y - MINY + PAD) * SCALE


def ink_bbox(img, thresh=128):
    """Bounding box of dark pixels."""
    g = img.convert("L")
    w, h = g.size
    px = g.load()
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = w, h, -1, -1
    for yy in range(h):
        for xx in range(w):
            if px[xx, yy] < thresh:
                if xx < x0: x0 = xx
                if yy < y0: y0 = yy
                if xx > x1: x1 = xx
                if yy > y1: y1 = yy
    if x1 < 0:
        return None
    return (x0, y0, x1 + 1, y1 + 1)


def render(text, size):
    f = ImageFont.truetype(FONT, size)
    tmp = Image.new("RGB", (3000, 300), "white")
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(tmp)
    d.text((100, 100), text, font=f, fill=(28, 28, 30))
    bb = ink_bbox(tmp)
    return tmp.crop(bb), bb

---
name: kenny-boyd-doc-review-preferences
description: Kenny Boyd's editorial constraints on Athletics policy/framework docs — no language implying past incompetence, no judgmental tier labels, name the seniority of reviewers
metadata:
  type: project
---

Kenny Boyd (reviewer on the Baylor Athletics Software and Technology Management
Framework) consistently pushes back on three things in draft policy language:

1. **No language that implies the department was previously incompetent.** He cut
   "so the department stops discovering it is in the final year of an agreement
   with no time to act" for exactly this reason. Rewrite as forward-looking
   capability ("advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to
   evaluate options"), not as a problem being fixed.
2. **No judgmental or ranking-flavored labels.** He rejected the Light / Standard /
   Elevated review tiers. Neutral, descriptive, escalating names work better —
   Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive Review. He floated
   Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, which reads as sophistication of the
   *technology* rather than depth of *review*.
3. **Name the seniority of the reviewer, not just the office.** For ITS he wanted
   it clear that a supervisory-level person with authority to commit resources is
   involved, not a line technician. Frame this as decision authority the request
   requires, never as competence of the staff.

He also wants Baylor branding carried through headers/footers and draft status
marked on every page.

**Why:** These are tone constraints, not content ones — the same facts land or
fail on phrasing. Getting them wrong costs a full review cycle.

**How to apply:** Before sending any Athletics policy or framework draft for his
review, scan for blame-implying rationale, ranking adjectives on process tiers,
and unqualified office names where seniority matters.

"""Shared Baylor Athletics document styling.

Matches the JA policy scan: green page border, running header/footer, dark-green
table headers with hairline rules, Aptos throughout.
"""
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor, Emu
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

FONT = "Aptos"
BAYLOR_GREEN = "154734"
GREY = "595959"
RULE = "D9D9D9"


class Doc:
    def __init__(self, footer_text):
        self.doc = Document()
        s = self.doc.sections[0]
        s.page_width, s.page_height = Emu(7772400), Emu(10058400)
        s.left_margin = s.right_margin = s.top_margin = s.bottom_margin = Emu(457200)
        self.section = s

        normal = self.doc.styles["Normal"]
        normal.font.name = FONT
        normal.font.size = Pt(10.5)
        normal.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), FONT)
        normal.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
        normal.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)

        self._page_border(s)
        self._header(s)
        self._footer(s, footer_text)

    # ---------- chrome ----------
    def _page_border(self, section, color=BAYLOR_GREEN, sz=8, space=20):
        pgb = OxmlElement("w:pgBorders")
        pgb.set(qn("w:offsetFrom"), "page")
        for edge in ("top", "left", "bottom", "right"):
            b = OxmlElement(f"w:{edge}")
            b.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
            b.set(qn("w:sz"), str(sz))
            b.set(qn("w:space"), str(space))
            b.set(qn("w:color"), color)
            pgb.append(b)
        section._sectPr.append(pgb)

    def _header(self, s):
        p = s.header.paragraphs[0]
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
        r = p.add_run("Draft for discussion  |  Baylor Athletics")
        r.font.name, r.font.size, r.font.bold = FONT, Pt(9), True
        r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(BAYLOR_GREEN)

    def _field(self, paragraph, instr):
        r = paragraph.add_run()
        beg = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); beg.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "begin")
        it = OxmlElement("w:instrText"); it.set(qn("xml:space"), "preserve"); it.text = f" {instr} "
        end = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); end.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "end")
        r._r.append(beg); r._r.append(it); r._r.append(end)
        return r

    def _footer(self, s, text):
        p = s.footer.paragraphs[0]
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
        r = p.add_run(text)
        r.font.name, r.font.size = FONT, Pt(8.5)
        r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(BAYLOR_GREEN)

        pg = s.footer.add_paragraph()
        pg.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
        pg.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
        for txt in ("Page ",):
            rr = pg.add_run(txt); rr.font.name, rr.font.size = FONT, Pt(8.5)
            rr.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GREY)
        f1 = self._field(pg, "PAGE")
        f1.font.name, f1.font.size = FONT, Pt(8.5)
        f1.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GREY)
        rr = pg.add_run(" of "); rr.font.name, rr.font.size = FONT, Pt(8.5)
        rr.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GREY)
        f2 = self._field(pg, "NUMPAGES")
        f2.font.name, f2.font.size = FONT, Pt(8.5)
        f2.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GREY)

    # ---------- text ----------
    def para(self, text="", size=10.5, bold=False, italic=False, color=None,
             space_before=0, space_after=6, style=None, align=None):
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
        if align is not None:
            p.alignment = align
        if text:
            r = p.add_run(text)
            r.font.name, r.font.size = FONT, Pt(size)
            r.font.bold, r.font.italic = bold, italic
            if color:
                r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
        return p

    def title(self, main, sub=None, eyebrow="BAYLOR ATHLETICS"):
        if eyebrow:
            self.para(eyebrow, size=11, bold=True, color=BAYLOR_GREEN, space_after=1)
        self.para(main, size=19, bold=True, color=BAYLOR_GREEN, space_after=2)
        if sub:
            self.para(sub, size=13, bold=True, color=GREY, space_after=10)

    def h1(self, text):
        p = self.para(text, size=14.5, bold=True, color=BAYLOR_GREEN,
                      space_before=15, space_after=6)
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
        return p

    def h2(self, text):
        p = self.para(text, size=12, bold=True, color=BAYLOR_GREEN,
                      space_before=10, space_after=4)
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
        return p

    def bullet(self, text, size=10.5, bold_lead=None):
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
        if bold_lead:
            r = p.add_run(bold_lead)
            r.font.name, r.font.size, r.font.bold = FONT, Pt(size), True
            r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(BAYLOR_GREEN)
        r = p.add_run(text)
        r.font.name, r.font.size = FONT, Pt(size)
        return p

    # ---------- tables ----------
    def _look(self, t):
        tblPr = t._tbl.tblPr
        borders = OxmlElement("w:tblBorders")
        for edge in ("top", "left", "bottom", "right", "insideH", "insideV"):
            b = OxmlElement(f"w:{edge}")
            b.set(qn("w:val"), "single"); b.set(qn("w:sz"), "4")
            b.set(qn("w:space"), "0"); b.set(qn("w:color"), RULE)
            borders.append(b)
        tblPr.append(borders)
        mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
        for edge, val in (("top", "80"), ("bottom", "80"), ("left", "120"), ("right", "120")):
            m = OxmlElement(f"w:{edge}")
            m.set(qn("w:w"), val); m.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
            mar.append(m)
        tblPr.append(mar)

    def _shade(self, cell, hexcolor):
        tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
        shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
        shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
        shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hexcolor)
        tcPr.append(shd)

    def table(self, headers, rows, widths=None, keep_together=False, size=9.5):
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
        t.style = "Table Grid"
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
        hdr = t.rows[0]
        trPr = hdr._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
        th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); th.set(qn("w:val"), "true")
        trPr.append(th)
        for i, htext in enumerate(headers):
            cell = hdr.cells[i]; cell.text = ""
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            r = p.add_run(htext)
            r.font.name, r.font.size, r.font.bold = FONT, Pt(size), True
            r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("FFFFFF")
            self._shade(cell, BAYLOR_GREEN)
        for row in rows:
            cells = t.add_row().cells
            for i, val in enumerate(row):
                cells[i].text = ""
                p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]
                p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
                r = p.add_run(val)
                r.font.name, r.font.size = FONT, Pt(size)
        for row in t.rows:
            rPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
            rPr.append(OxmlElement("w:cantSplit"))
        if widths:
            for row in t.rows:
                for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                    row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
        if keep_together:
            for row in t.rows[:-1]:
                for c in row.cells:
                    for p in c.paragraphs:
                        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
        self._look(t)
        self.para("", space_after=2)
        return t

    def meta_table(self, rows, widths):
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=2)
        t.style = "Table Grid"
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
        for label, val in rows:
            cells = t.add_row().cells
            for i, text in enumerate((label, val)):
                cells[i].text = ""
                p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]
                p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
                r = p.add_run(text)
                r.font.name, r.font.size = FONT, Pt(9.5)
                if i == 0:
                    r.font.bold = True
                    r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(BAYLOR_GREEN)
        for row in t.rows:
            rPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
            rPr.append(OxmlElement("w:cantSplit"))
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
        self._look(t)
        self.para("", space_after=2)
        return t

    def picture(self, path, height_in):
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph()
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
        p.add_run().add_picture(path, height=Inches(height_in))
        return p

    def page_break(self):
        self.doc.add_page_break()

    def save(self, path):
        self.doc.save(path)
        print("WROTE:", path)

"""Executive summary — condensed from the merged framework. No new claims."""
from baylordoc import Doc, WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH

OUT = "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/Software_and_Tech_Management_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-08-11.docx"

d = Doc("Software and Technology Management Framework  ·  Executive Summary  ·  Baylor Athletics  ·  Draft")

d.title("Software and Technology Management Framework", "Executive Summary")

d.meta_table(
    [
        ("Status", "Draft for discussion"),
        ("Date", "August 11, 2026"),
        ("Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"),
        ("Companion documents",
         "Software and Technology Management Framework (full); Request Workflow; "
         "Technology Idea Form; Internal ATH Form; Technology Evaluation Scorecard; "
         "Request Tracker"),
    ],
    widths=[1.6, 5.9],
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- in brief
d.h1("In brief")
d.para(
    "Requests for software and technology currently move at different speeds through "
    "different channels depending on who initiates them. This framework establishes one "
    "route for every request: a single intake, two control points in a fixed order, a "
    "named point of contact, a review depth matched to the risk the request carries, and a "
    "scheduled decision on whether to renew."
)
d.para(
    "It is department-wide and covers all software and technology, in every unit. Athlete "
    "performance technology sits inside that scope as the category carrying the most "
    "sensitive data, and it triggers the deepest review."
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- why
d.h1("Why this framework")
d.bullet(
    "Technology used in athletics can collect biometric, health-related, performance, "
    "workload, recovery, video, sensor, and survey data. Responsible use requires "
    "coordination across Athletics, Sports Medicine, ITS, Privacy, Legal, Compliance, "
    "Procurement, and Records Management — no single unit can carry the decision alone."
)
d.bullet(
    "The NCAA Sports Science Institute has published guidance on the responsible use of "
    "performance technologies. That guidance is high-level by design and leaves "
    "implementation to each school. This framework is Baylor Athletics' implementation."
)
d.bullet(
    "The department needs a shared view of what it already owns, when agreements end, and "
    "whether what was purchased is actually being used."
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- what changes
d.h1("What it establishes")
d.bullet(
    "for every request — the Technology Idea Form and the internal ATH Form, declaring the "
    "data category and the proposed review level at the point of intake.",
    bold_lead="One intake ",
)
d.bullet(
    ", in order — the Business Office first for budget, contract, and duplication; then ITS "
    "for technical, security, and integration review. A request is purchased only after "
    "both have cleared it, and declined requests come back with documented reasons.",
    bold_lead="Two control points",
)
d.bullet(
    " — the Director of Applied Performance facilitates, holds a weekly standing meeting "
    "with ITS on all open requests, and gives regular status updates. Requesters are not "
    "asked to chase their own request.",
    bold_lead="One point of contact",
)
d.bullet(
    " — three levels, from a light compliance and privacy check through to full review with "
    "Health & Wellness and medical sign-off.",
    bold_lead="Review depth that scales",
)
d.bullet(
    " — every product is reviewed at six months or the end of the competitive season, "
    "whichever is longer. The outcome is renew, renegotiate, or discontinue.",
    bold_lead="A scheduled decision",
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- phases
d.h1("How a request moves")
d.table(
    ["Phase", "What happens", "Who owns it"],
    [
        ("Phase 1\nProposal, approval,\npurchase",
         "Intake forms completed and the review level declared. Business Office reviews, "
         "then ITS. The request is scored against the Technology Evaluation Scorecard and "
         "purchased only after both control points clear.",
         "Requester initiates;\nBusiness Office and ITS\nare the control points"),
        ("Phase 2\nImplementation and\nproduct use",
         "A project manager is assigned. The weekly ITS standing meeting tracks every open "
         "request, so each one has a known owner and a known blocker.",
         "Assigned Project Manager,\nfacilitated by the Director\nof Applied Performance"),
        ("Phase 3\nReview and\nrenewal decision",
         "Actual utilization is compared against the intent stated on the original request. "
         "Low utilization opens a diagnostic conversation before any renewal conclusion.",
         "Sport Administrator\nsigns off"),
    ],
    widths=[1.5, 3.9, 2.1],
    keep_together=True,
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- levels
d.h1("How deeply a request is reviewed")
d.table(
    ["Level", "Applies when", "Review includes"],
    [
        ("Level 1\nStandard Review", "No athlete data; single unit; low or one-time cost",
         "Compliance, Privacy, Ownership, Transparency, Interoperability"),
        ("Level 2\nEnhanced Review", "Performance data, multi-team use, or recurring cost",
         "Full review"),
        ("Level 3\nComprehensive Review",
         "Physiologic or health data; external data sharing; third-party processing of "
         "athlete data",
         "Full review, plus data protection review and Health & Wellness / medical sign-off"),
    ],
    widths=[1.3, 2.7, 3.5],
    keep_together=True,
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exceptions
d.h1("Exceptions")
d.para(
    "Urgent requests use an expedited lane, not a bypass. They clear the same two control "
    "points on a compressed clock, with a short risk checklist completed at intake. A "
    "request directed by an administrative lead enters that lane on receipt, which gives a "
    "clear and documented gate for what qualifies as urgent rather than leaving it to be "
    "argued case by case."
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- status
d.h1("Where it stands")
d.para(
    "This is a draft for discussion. The full framework carries the policy statement, "
    "scope, definitions, and the complete roles and responsibilities table, and routes "
    "athlete performance technology decisions into existing Baylor governance channels "
    "rather than around them. Final policy language should be reviewed by the Office of "
    "General Counsel, University Compliance and Risk Services, ITS, and Privacy."
)

d.save(OUT)

    text_all = " ".join(lines); text_mine = " ".join(mine)
    print(f"=== {name} ===  units:{len(lines)}  not-verbatim-from-your-draft:{len(mine)}")
    def rep(label, pat, flags=0):
        a=len(re.findall(pat, text_all, flags)); m=len(re.findall(pat, text_mine, flags))
        print(f"   {label:<26} total:{a:<3} in text I wrote:{m}")
    rep("em dash", r'—')
    rep("AI vocabulary", AI_VOCAB, re.I)
    rep("conjunctive openers", CONJ, re.M)
    rep("superficial -ing", ING, re.I)
    rep("vague attribution", VAGUE, re.I)
    rep("negative parallelism", NEGPAR)
    print()

print("=== every negative parallelism, with origin ===")
for name in ('MERGED','EXEC_SUMMARY','WORKFLOW'):
    for l in load(f'chk_{name}.txt'):
        for m in re.finditer(NEGPAR, l):
            origin = "YOUR DRAFT" if re.sub(r'\s+',' ',l) in src else "I wrote/adapted"
            print(f"  [{name:<12}] ({origin}) ...{m.group(0)[:95]}")
